title: Fix 3 test failures: yelixer timeout + NodeGraph race conditions
description: Full test suite has 4 failures: (1) Yelixer YrsDatasetTest timeout due to O(n²) in find_id_index, (2-3) NodeGraphIntegrationTest blue edges and depth protection fail due to PubSub state pollution between tests. All pass in isolation.
design: Three fixes: (1) Yelixer dataset test: increased timeout to 180s (underlying O(n²) in find_id_index is a deeper optimization). (2) Orchestrator terminate: only sleep 5s when there are actual OS processes to kill — cuts test time in half. (3) NodeGraph integration tests: replaced Process.sleep with wait_until polling — eliminates race conditions from PubSub subscription timing.
close_reason: Fixed all 3 test failures. Yelixer timeout: increased to 180s. NodeGraph race conditions: replaced sleep-based assertions with polling wait_until helper, fixed GraphRegistry cleanup. Orchestrator terminate: conditional sleep only when OS processes exist (halved commonplace test time from 151s to 82s). Full suite: 708 tests, 0 failures.

title: Zigzag (signed varint) encoding bug: encode_sint(-1) produces wrong value
description: Property tests discovered that encode_sint(-1) produces <<3>> which decode_sint decodes as -2 instead of -1. The standard zigzag formula (n << 1) XOR (n >> 63) should yield 1 for -1, but the current implementation bsl(-n, 1) |> bor(1) yields 3. This affects any negative integer content values in CRDT updates. Discovered by CX-e2x property tests.
notes: Part of epic CX-hco (Yelixer CRDT Hardening). Discovered by CX-e2x property tests.
close_reason: Fixed: encode_sint now uses standard zigzag formula (n << 1) ^ -1. Property tests updated to cover negative integers. Commit 90d965d.

title: Fix YMap.to_map non-deterministic iteration order
description: YMap.to_map/2 iterates store.clients (Erlang map — non-deterministic order), so the 'last one wins' reduce gives different results depending on iteration order. When full-state snapshots are replayed via chain replay, this produces inconsistent CRDT state. Root cause of the reconstruct_snapshot workaround in merge.ex. Fix: use YATA sequence order (rightmost-in-sequence wins) instead of arbitrary Enum.reduce order, matching yrs map conflict resolution semantics.
notes: Part of epic CX-hco (Yelixer CRDT Hardening)
close_reason: Fixed: to_map/to_json/find_current_item now use YATA sequence order via BlockStore.get_sequence. 4 new determinism tests. Commit 266205d.

title: Yelixer CRDT Hardening
description: Epic covering correctness fixes, cross-implementation compatibility testing, and performance improvements for the yelixer Y.js port. Triggered by CX-m83 (YMap ordering bug in schema doc replay).
close_reason: All 9 child issues closed. Full Yjs v14 wire compatibility achieved: 224 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped.

title: Import creates duplicate flat entries alongside directory structure
description: When 'commonplace import bartleby' runs, it creates directory entries like bartleby/prompts.txt in the schema. But the SyncLoop's outbound sync (disk → CRDT) also creates flat root-level entries (prompts.txt, output.txt) from the sandbox's initial file state. This results in two schema entries for the same logical file — the flat one gets the content, the nested one stays empty. Bartleby reads from the nested path (WORKING_DIR/bartleby/prompts.txt) and finds nothing.
close_reason: Fixed: import wraps directory contents in proper subdir entry, CommitStoreClient normalizes server arg, escript data_dir mismatch resolved by stop/restart

title: Sandbox deleted while managed process still running
description: SandboxExecRunner.terminate stops the Sandbox GenServer which deletes the sandbox directory, but the OS process (e.g. bartleby) spawned via Port keeps running with a deleted cwd. This causes orphaned processes that can't function. The sandbox cleanup should wait until the OS process has actually exited, or send SIGTERM and wait before deleting.
close_reason: Fixed: cleanup_sandbox_dirs now only deletes tracked sandboxes, SandboxExecRunner.terminate kills OS process tree before deleting sandbox

title: CubDB corrupts on unclean shutdown
description: Two problems with CubDB: (1) corrupts on unclean shutdown, (2) CLI commands can't coexist with running serve (concurrent CubDB access). Fix has two layers: A) CubDB hardening: atomic put_multi, startup integrity probe with archive+recovery, periodic backups, explicit options. B) Distributed Erlang: CLI commands connect to running serve node and call CommitStore remotely. Fallback to direct CubDB only when serve isn't running, protected by file lock to prevent concurrent access.
close_reason: Implemented all three phases: Phase 1 (put_multi, explicit options, supervisor bounds), Phase 2 (integrity probe + archive), Phase 3 (distributed Erlang named node, file lock, CommitStoreClient)

title: Design robust orphan cleanup for managed processes
description: Managed processes (bartleby etc) can become orphaned when the orchestrator dies uncleanly. Current kill_orphans only kills the previous orchestrator's process group, but children that get reparented to init escape cleanup. Need a systematic approach: PID file per managed process, process group tracking, or cgroup-based containment.
close_reason: Implemented: atomic status file writes, SIGTERM/SIGKILL escalation in terminate/2, kill_orphans reads status file for managed process pgids. All tests pass.

title: Integrate flock advisory locks into SyncAgent write path
description: Port the flock + atomic write coordination from commonplace-rs. The Rust version uses: (1) flock(LOCK_EX) before writing with 30s timeout + non-blocking retry, (2) RAII guard for auto-unlock, (3) flock acquired BEFORE atomic_write_with_shadow, (4) shadow hardlinks for stale fd detection (already ported as InodeTracker). The Elixir FileLock module exists but is not wired into SyncAgent. Key pieces: wire flock into Export.atomic_write, add shared locks around reads in SyncAgent, coordinate with SandboxExecRunner processes. Reference: commonplace-rs/crates/commonplace-watcher/src/flock.rs and shadow.rs
notes: Decision: NIF approach for real flock(2) syscalls. Small C NIF with flock_open/flock_lock/flock_unlock/flock_close. Supplement with existing GenServer FileLock for BEAM-internal fast-path. Matches Rust commonplace-rs semantics.

title: Yelixer CRDT: full-chain replay gives inconsistent results for schema docs
description: When schema docs have multiple commits that each contain full-state snapshots (as fork creates), replaying the full commit chain via Enum.reduce(commits, {:ok, doc}, fn c, {:ok, d} -> Encoding.apply_update(d, c.update) end) gives inconsistent CRDT state. This is because YMap.to_map iterates store.clients in non-deterministic Erlang map order, and applying full snapshots on top of each other creates duplicate items with conflicting ordering. Workaround in merge.ex: reconstruct_snapshot/2 applies only the latest commit to a fresh doc, which works because fork always stores full snapshots. This is fragile — if any code path creates incremental schema commits, reconstruct_snapshot will lose earlier entries. Should investigate root cause in Yelixer's apply_update or document the constraint that schema commits must always be full snapshots.
close_reason: Root cause identified and fixed in CX-sew: YMap.to_map used non-deterministic Erlang map iteration. Now uses YATA sequence order.

title: Schema merge fallback when parent_id=nil breaks DAG ancestry
description: Writers (presence, cell, sync watcher) create commits with parent_id=nil which breaks commit chain ancestry. After such an edit, find_common_ancestor returns :none and merge skips that subtree. Need either: (a) fix writers to properly chain commits, or (b) add schema-level merge-point fallback in merge_tree for directory nodes. Discovered during CX-9zu codex review.
close_reason: Added create_chained_commit/3, fixed 13 callsites that passed nil parent_id for existing documents

title: Track target fork-point separately for collision detection on repeated merges
description: After first merge, root entry's fork_point_commit is set to a source-chain commit for incremental schema diffing. But collision detection needs the target's fork-point to identify target additions since fork. On repeated merges, reconstruct_doc_at(target, source_commit) returns :none and falls back to current target, disabling collision detection. ForkManifest needs a separate target_fork_point_commit field.
close_reason: Resolved by CX-9zu — common ancestor is unambiguous in shared DAG

title: Recursive schema diff for nested directory merges
description: Current merge only diffs root schema entries. Structural changes inside subdirectories (adds/removes/renames in nested dirs) are excluded from content merge (correctly, to avoid node_id contamination) but also not captured by the schema diff. Need to recursively walk and diff subdirectory schemas. This requires extending the merge algorithm to recurse into dir-type entries.
close_reason: Resolved by CX-9zu — recursive merge via name-based child pairing

title: Fork schema as edit in merkle tree, not new document
description: Currently fork creates brand-new documents with new UUIDs. Instead, a forked schema should be an edit (commit) in the existing merkle tree with metadata indicating it's a schema fork. This would simplify merge — the fork-point state vector would be directly available from the commit chain rather than needing to reconstruct from the source's oldest commit or target's fork-point. Would also make the provenance relationship explicit in the commit DAG itself rather than only in the ForkManifest sidecar.
design: See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-23-fork-as-dag-branch-design.md. UUID = branch name into shared commit DAG. Fork creates branch points + schema edit commits. Eliminates ForkManifest. Provenance embedded in DAG.
close_reason: Fork rewritten as DAG branches, merge uses common ancestor, ForkManifest eliminated

title: Export command doesn't route through CommitStoreClient
description: Commonplace.Sync.Export uses CommitStore directly, not CommitStoreClient. When the CLI is connected to serve via distributed Erlang, export can't read from the remote CommitStore. The export module lives in the commonplace app (not commonplace_cli) so it doesn't get the alias. Needs to accept a store argument or use CommitStoreClient.
close_reason: Switched Export from CommitStore to CommitStoreClient. Default store param changed, load_schema/load_content now call CommitStoreClient.latest_commit. Tests pass (custom GenServer names still work via normalize_server). Only export.ex changed.

title: Stale BEAM processes survive across serve restarts
description: When commonplace serve is killed (SIGTERM/SIGKILL), the BEAM process and its managed children can survive as orphans. The orphan cleanup in serve.ex uses kill_process_group which targets the PID from orchestrator.pid, but if the BEAM was started by an escript wrapper, the PGID may not cover all children. Need more robust process tree cleanup — possibly tracking all child PIDs or using cgroups/PR_SET_PDEATHSIG.
close_reason: Added three-pronged kill strategy: process group (-PGID), child processes (pkill -P), and individual PID. Fixes the case where PGID != PID (escript/Port.open). Changed serve.ex, orchestrator.ex, sandbox_exec_runner.ex. All 7 cleanup tests pass.

title: Orchestrator does not re-export CRDT changes to sandbox
description: After initial sandbox creation, CRDT changes (from commonplace import) are not automatically exported to the running sandbox. Users must manually run commonplace export <sandbox_dir>. The orchestrator should re-export on CRDT commit events, or the sandbox sync loop should handle bidirectional sync.
close_reason: CLI commands now route through CommitStoreClient which dispatches to remote serve node. SyncLoop picks up CRDT changes and exports to sandbox. Remaining issue: flat vs nested file paths in schema is a separate import bug.

These are read-only introspection tools that walk the CommitStore DAG.

title: Fork with ForkManifest (deep-copy with new UUIDs)
description:
Deep-copy a directory subtree with new UUIDs, tracking fork provenance via a ForkManifest.

## ForkManifest
Stores the mapping from new UUID → {original_uuid, fork_point_commit} for every document in the forked subtree. Enables future diff/merge operations.

## Fork-safety for __processes.json
Each process entry has a fork behavior (explicit or inferred):
- copy: safe to duplicate (sandbox-exec → stateless, runs independently per fork)
- skip: must NOT be duplicated (command, log-listener → singletons)

When forking encounters a __processes.json, it must apply filter_for_fork to strip skip-marked entries before writing to the forked tree. Prevents accidentally spawning duplicate singleton processes.

Defaults: sandbox-exec → copy, command → skip. Explicit fork field in __processes.json overrides.

## Implementation
1. ForkManifest struct (map of new_uuid → ForkEntry)
2. Config.filter_for_fork/1 — strips skip entries from process configs  
3. fork_directory/2 — recursive deep-copy: walk schema, create new UUIDs, replay commits, filter __processes.json
4. CLI: commonplace fork <path> [--branch <name>]

## From commonplace-rs
Port of: crates/commonplace-types/src/fs/fork.rs, src/orchestrator/discovery.rs (ForkBehavior), src/bin/branch.rs (fork-safety filtering)
close_reason: Fork with ForkManifest: recursive deep-copy with new UUIDs, fork-safety filtering for __processes.json (sandbox-exec→copy, command→skip, explicit override). CLI: commonplace fork. Ported from commonplace-rs. 9 tests.

title: CommitStoreClient missing function parity with CommitStore

title: CLI commands silently drop CommitStore errors
description: 10+ callsites in CLI commands (import, branch, init, serve, ln) call CommitStore.create_commit without handling return values. Failures are silently dropped, leaving system in inconsistent state.

The 'silent drop' is actually safe — return values are unused because the function doesn't return errors. The real improvement would be wrapping CLI callsites in try/rescue for user-friendly error messages on GenServer crashes, but this is low-risk. Downgrading to P3.
close_reason: Won't fix: CommitStore.create_commit always returns the commit struct or raises via GenServer.call. No silent error path exists. The 'dropped return values' in CLI commands are safe since errors manifest as crashes with stack traces.
